hero.title: The harness for your AI fabric
hero.description: KubeRocketCI is an open-source, Kubernetes-native delivery platform. Engineers and their AI agents ship through one golden path: opinionated pipelines, quality gates, and ephemeral environments.

aiFabric.title: The harness for AI fabrics
aiFabric.description: Pipelines and quality gates didn't vanish in the agentic era — they became its control point. Agent fleets need exactly what a mature delivery platform does best.

harness.title: Execution harness
harness.description: Agents iterate at machine speed. Give every change — human or agent — the same loop: opinionated Tekton pipelines, automated reviews, and quality gates that turn agent output into evidence-backed, mergeable results.

guardrails.title: Guardrails by default
guardrails.description: Route agents down the same golden path as your developers. RBAC, policy-aware self-service, and a GitOps audit trail make every agent action a reviewable commit — governance built in, not bolted on.

ephemeral.title: Ephemeral velocity
ephemeral.description: Validate hypotheses cheaply. Spin up an isolated, production-like environment per task, run the experiment, promote what passes the gates, and tear the rest down clean.

platform.title: How the harness works
platform.description: Everything runs on your Kubernetes cluster, with configuration stored as code in Git.

goldenPath.title: One golden path
goldenPath.description: One road from commit to production: predefined pipelines and self-service that developers and AI agents share, so every change follows the same path.

gates.title: Quality gates and security
gates.description: Quality gates, code and vulnerability scanners, and RBAC guardrails are built into every pipeline, with single sign-on through OIDC or SAML.

openSource.title: Open source and Kubernetes-native
openSource.description: Runs on any Kubernetes cluster and any cloud, built on open-source CNCF tooling and operated through an intuitive UI and API.

quickStart.title: Up and running in hours
quickStart.description: Application templates and predefined pipelines let you scaffold a new service, or migrate an existing one to a CI/CD flow, in a few hours.

aiFactory.title: From CI/CD platform to AI factory
aiFactory.descriptionLead: KubeRocketCI is an open-source, Kubernetes-native delivery platform: one golden path for engineers and their AI agents.
aiFactory.description: As agent fleets multiply delivery demand, it supplies the gates, guardrails, and disposable environments they need.

shift.title: The layer that didn't vanish
shift.paragraph1: When coding agents arrived, some predicted pipelines and quality gates would fade away. Instead, every agent-opened pull request now triggers a pipeline, a review, a scan, and a deployment. The delivery layer became the control point of the whole factory.
shift.paragraph2: Agents get things wrong at machine speed. A fabric compounds value only when each hypothesis gets a guardrailed environment, runs the gates, promotes what passes, and destroys the rest.
shift.warning: of agentic AI projects will be canceled by 2027 over governance gaps, Gartner predicts.
shift.warningSource: 40%: Gartner Hype Cycle for Platform Engineering, 2026.
shift.survivors: The platforms that survive route agents through the same golden paths as humans.

needs.title: What an AI fabric needs from its factory
needs.description: Six capabilities separate a fleet that ships from a fleet that floods your review queue.

harness.title: Execution harness
harness.description: A standing loop every change runs through: build, test, lint, scan, review. Agents produce output; the harness turns it into evidence.

qualityGates.title: Quality gates
qualityGates.description: Autotests and code-quality thresholds decide what gets promoted. When changes arrive at machine speed, the gate — not the author — is the trust boundary.

guardrails.title: Guardrails and governance
guardrails.description: Agents get the same identity and RBAC boundaries as every developer, with no side door around the paved road.

auditTrail.title: Audit trail by design
auditTrail.description: Every configuration and every change lives in Git as a commit, so whatever an agent changes is reviewable and revertible.

ephemeral.title: Ephemeral environments
ephemeral.description: A disposable, production-like environment per hypothesis: create, validate, tear down clean. No agent waits for a shared staging slot.

observability.title: Fleet observability
observability.description: Logs, metrics, and alerts across every pipeline run — so you notice drift and flakiness before they compound.

delivery.description: No roadmap promises — each capability maps to a platform feature you can use right now.

harness.description: Predefined Tekton pipelines for polyglot microservices, plus custom pipelines when your flow needs its own steps.

qualityGates.description: Autotests as quality gates in CD pipelines — reliable versions get promoted, failures stop at the gate.

guardrails.description: Single Sign-On with OIDC/SAML identity providers and Kubernetes RBAC across the whole platform.

auditTrail.description: The GitOps approach stores platform and application configuration as code in Git — every change is a commit.

ephemeral.description: Deploy any feature branch into its own environment, test it deeply, and destroy it when the hypothesis is answered.

observability.description: Logging, monitoring, and alerting stacks with code-quality and vulnerability scanning built into the platform.

cta.title: Put your agents through the gate
cta.subtitle: Walk through the golden path in a demo. The core is open source, so you can inspect it first.

aiSdlc.title: The baseline your AI SDLC runs on
aiSdlc.description: Code is no longer the bottleneck. Proving it is. KubeRocketCI gives every change, from an agent or an engineer, the same loops, quality gates, and ephemeral environments, whatever tool runs in each phase.
aiSdlc.layersSummary: The platform is what every change runs through. The AI layer is the agents, skills, and workflows on top, ours or yours.
aiSdlc.storyLabel: The seven phases of an AI SDLC and where KubeRocketCI helps in each

plan.title: Plan: spec-driven, your way
plan.description: Specs live in Git and trace through to the version and environment that runs them. Bring the spec-driven approach your team already uses. Our agents and skills follow one too, from brief to requirements, epics, and stories, each approved before the next.

design.title: Design: decisions before code
design.description: Application templates give every new service a known starting point, and ephemeral environments let you try a design as a prototype before you commit to it. An architect agent turns approved stories into an architecture and a feature plan across repositories, then reviews the design against your standards.

build.title: Build: every push runs the same pipeline
build.description: A webhook on every push starts the same predefined pipeline for agents and engineers, and agents read the results through the CLI. Developer agents work with skills for your stack and workflows that take an issue to a pull request.
build.workflows: Implement a feature, fix an issue

test.title: Test: prove it in its own environment
test.description: Each change can run in an ephemeral environment, and autotests act as quality gates. QA agents write test plans, test cases, and automated tests, and a workflow verifies the change on a live cluster.
test.workflows: Verify a change on a test cluster

review.title: Review: the gate is the trust boundary
review.description: Every pull request runs a review pipeline with code quality and security scans, and only changes that pass every check reach a human. A review agent checks the change against your conventions, and merge rights stay with people.
review.workflows: Review a change, write the commit

deploy.title: Deploy: agents propose, the pipeline applies
deploy.description: Deployment Flows promote what passed the gates from one environment to the next through GitOps. Manual or autotest gates guard each promotion, RBAC decides who approves, and every release traces back to its story. Agents propose through the same flow, and workflows draft release notes and upgrade guides.
deploy.skills: Trace a story to its environment

operate.title: Operate: learnings feed the next plan
operate.description: Observability covers every pipeline run and environment, and agent telemetry shows token cost per story. A skill explains why an environment is unhealthy or out of sync and who owns the fix. What you learn goes back into Plan.
operate.workflows: Reproduce, fix, and verify an issue

own.title: Ours, yours, or both
own.description: Use our agents, skills, and workflows, bring the ones your team already has, or build custom ones to deliver other solutions on the platform. The phases and the platform underneath stay the same.
own.agents: Use ours or bring your own
own.workflows: Build custom ones for other solutions

secretsManagement.title: Keep secrets out of your pipelines
secretsManagement.description: Use an external secret store to handle sensitive data safely across namespaces, including database connections in development and deployment.

autotestQualityGate.title: Let autotests decide what ships
autotestQualityGate.description: Run autotests as a quality gate in the deployment pipeline to verify stability before promotion. The same gate checks agent-generated code.

envVariables.title: Tune test runs without changing test code
envVariables.description: Add, change or remove test suite parameters through environment variables in CD pipelines, so one gate adapts to different environments.

customPipelines.title: Adapt the pipelines to your project
customPipelines.description: Start from the pre-configured Tekton pipelines and create custom ones that fit your project's requirements.

featureBranch.title: Test a feature branch in its own environment
featureBranch.description: Deploy a feature branch to a separate environment and test it without touching the main branch. It works for hypotheses proposed by AI agents too.
